newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lufthansa to cooperate with Belgian VLM.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to cooperate with Belgian VLM.

text.p: German carrier Lufhansa has reached an operational cooperation deal with Belgian Vlaamse Luchtvaart Maatschappij, Antwerp-based VLM said on Tuesday.
VLM sales and marketing manager Herman Vermeiren declined to give details of the deal, which will be presented at a news conference in Antwerp on Wednesday.

Lufthansa declined to comment. In an invitation for the conference it said it would "present the planned short-term initiatives of our company aimed at strengthening our position on the Benelux market".
VLM, owned by Dutch entrepeneur Jaap Rosen Jacobsen, operates scheduled flights from the Antwerp, Rotterdam and Muenchengladbach airports to London City.

Founded in May 1992 and operational from May 1993, VLM currently has seven Fokker 50 aircraft and has ordered two more. Three of the seven turboprop planes are leased to Spanish independent regional airline Air Nostrum.
VLM and Lufthansa declined to say whether their deal would allow Lufthansa to compete with KLM of the Netherlands on the Rotterdam-London route.

Belgian Sabena has a code-sharing deal with VLM for flights from Antwerp to London City Airport but Sabena spokesman Erik Sclep told Reuters that the VLM-Lufthansa deal was unlikely to have any impact on Sabena.
Sabena/VLM fly five times a day from Antwerp to London City and back on normal weekdays.
